# MEMORANDUM

**To:** [Supervising Partner]
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 10, 2026
**Re:** Drulun Therapeutics, Inc. / Pruvax Biologics Manufacturing, LLC: where Drulun stands under the current contract documents

**Privileged & Confidential: Attorney-Client Communication / Attorney Work Product**

---

## 1. Bottom Line

The documents contain three problems Drulun should raise with Pruvax. All three come from how the documents interact, not from any single document read alone. Ranked by importance to Drulun:

| Rank | Issue | Where | Exposure | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | Drulun's non-renewal notice was **10 days late**. The Supply Agreement has likely auto-renewed through **January 31, 2029**. | Order Form No. 3, Recital C, read with Supply Agreement §§ 2.1, 2.2 | Two more Contract Years at a **60,000-vial Annual Minimum**. Shortfall liability of up to about **US$8.65M per year** (about US$17.3M over the Renewal Term) at current pricing if Drulun orders nothing. | **Decision needed now.** The Initial Term expires January 31, 2027. |
| **2** | Order Form No. 3 redefines "Delivery" as **tender to the first carrier at Pruvax's Durham dock (FCA)**. Through the precedence clause, that overrides the Supply Agreement's "receipt in Edison, NJ." | Order Form No. 3, § 4.1, read with Supply Agreement §§ 1.7, 5.3, 6.2, 17.3 | Risk of loss and title on about **US$8.24M** of refrigerated product shift to Drulun **before cold-chain transit**. The 30-day rejection clock starts at Pruvax's dock. | **Action needed before the first batch ships** (OF3-01, requested delivery January 11, 2027). |
| **3** | The DPA selects **Delaware law and Delaware courts**, "notwithstanding" the Supply Agreement's New York choice. The precedence clause lets the DPA control on data matters. | DPA § 12, read with Supply Agreement §§ 15.1, 17.3 | A single serialization or complaint-handling failure could have to be litigated **in two forums under two bodies of law**. | Not time-critical. Fix it in the same amendment package. |

The **November 2023 draft** of the Supply Agreement is marked superseded, and its relevant provisions (Sections 1.7, 2.1, 2.2, 15.1 and 17.3) match the executed agreement. It gives Drulun no separate rights and changes nothing below. We should not rely on it.

---

## 2. Key Dates and Framework

- **Supply Agreement Effective Date:** February 1, 2024 (Supply Agreement preamble and § 1.8).
- **Initial Term:** three years from the Effective Date (§ 2.1). It ends **January 31, 2027**.
- **Renewal:** automatic for successive **two-year** Renewal Terms unless a Party gives written non-renewal notice under § 17.6 **at least 180 days before expiry** (§ 2.2). Notice is effective on receipt (§ 17.6).
- **Non-renewal deadline:** 180 days before January 31, 2027 is **August 4, 2026**.
- **Order of precedence (§ 17.3).** If the documents conflict:
  1. the **DPA** prevails on Personal Data matters;
  2. then the **Order Form** prevails on Products, quantities, pricing and delivery terms;
  3. then the Supply Agreement.

  This clause is what turns Issues 2 and 3 from drafting inconsistencies into terms that actually override the Supply Agreement.
- **Governing law and forum:** New York law; exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County (§ 15.1). There is also a jury waiver (§ 15.3) and executive escalation before litigation (§ 15.2).

---

## 3. Issues

### Issue 1 (Highest Priority, Decision Needed): Late Non-Renewal Notice and Likely Auto-Renewal

**Where:** Order Form No. 3 (dated September 8, 2026), **Recital C**. Read it with Supply Agreement §§ 2.1, 2.2, 3.4, 17.4 and 17.6, and Exhibit B.

**What the documents say**
- Recital C records that Drulun delivered a written Non-Renewal Notice **dated August 14, 2026**.
- The deadline under § 2.2 was **August 4, 2026**, so the notice was **untimely by at least 10 days**. Because notice is effective on receipt (§ 17.6), the actual receipt date may be later still.
- Recital C also states that "[e]ach Party reserves all rights regarding the effectiveness of the Non-Renewal Notice and the expiry or continuation of the Term," and that signing the Order Form waives no such right.

**Why it matters to Drulun**
- **Drulun is likely bound to a two-year Renewal Term, February 1, 2027 through January 31, 2029.** The renewal language is mechanical ("Renewal is automatic absent timely non-renewal notice"). The notice was not timely.
- **The Annual Minimum carries into the Renewal Term (§ 3.4; Exhibit B).**
  - Drulun must order and accept **60,000 vials per Contract Year**.
  - Any shortfall is invoiced at **35% of the then-current unit price**.
  - At the current US$412.00 price, that is **US$144.20 per vial short**. The maximum is about **US$8.65M per Contract Year**, or about **US$17.3M over the Renewal Term**, before any § 4.2 price increases.
- **Pruvax has preserved its position.** The mutual reservation in Recital C means Drulun has not conceded renewal. It also blocks any argument that Pruvax waived the deadline or is estopped by signing the Order Form. In addition, § 17.4 requires any waiver to be in writing and signed by the waiving Party.
- **New York General Obligations Law § 5-903 does not help.** That statute (which requires reminder notices before an automatic renewal can be enforced) applies to contracts for service, maintenance or repair. A finished-goods supply agreement is outside it.
- **Contractual exit routes are narrow.**
  - § 16.3 (regulatory termination) applies only if the FDA withdraws or suspends approval, or Drulun permanently discontinues U.S. commercialization.
  - § 16.1 requires an uncured material breach by Pruvax.
- **Bottom line:** Drulun's reserved position on effectiveness is **weak**. It should be treated as negotiating leverage, not as a defense to rely on.

**Recommended fix / next steps**
1. **Confirm the facts (this week).** Establish when and how the August 14 notice was actually sent and received, and whether the § 17.6 method was used (hand, overnight courier, or email with courier confirmation copy). Also check whether any **earlier written communication** from Drulun, sent on or before August 4, 2026, could itself qualify as a § 2.2 notice. That is the only realistic route to a timeliness argument.
2. **Negotiate with Pruvax before January 31, 2027.** In order of preference, seek:
   - a **written, signed waiver** of the § 2.2 deadline, accepting the August 14 notice as effective so the agreement expires January 31, 2027;
   - a **short-term extension** (for example, 6 to 12 months) in place of the two-year Renewal Term, with a reduced or pro-rated Annual Minimum;
   - if the Renewal Term stands, an amendment adding a **termination-for-convenience right** and **reducing or waiving the Annual Minimum and shortfall rate**.
3. **Possible leverage.** Issues 2 and 3 below, which favor Pruvax and are worth correcting, could be traded into one amendment package. Drulun's continuing volumes are another point of leverage.
4. **Planning assumption pending resolution.** Drulun should **plan and forecast as if it is bound through January 31, 2029**, including the 60,000-vial minimum. It should avoid any conduct that could be read as affirming renewal beyond what the existing Order Form requires.
5. **Fix the process.** Calendar the next non-renewal deadline at least 180 days before January 31, 2029, which is **August 4, 2028**. Build in a buffer and send notice by a § 17.6-compliant method.

> **Decision for Drulun:** Does it want to exit at January 31, 2027, or would it accept a shorter or modified continuation? This sets our negotiating ask and should be decided **promptly**. Each week closer to January 31 reduces Drulun's leverage.

---

### Issue 2 (High Priority, Action Before First Shipment): Order Form Redefines "Delivery" as Carrier Tender at Pruvax's Facility

**Where:** Order Form No. 3, **Section 4 (Delivery Terms), § 4.1**. Read it with Supply Agreement §§ 1.7, 5.3, 6.2, 10.2 and 17.3.

**What the documents say**
- **Supply Agreement § 1.7:** "Delivery" means receipt of Product at Drulun's designated distribution center in **Edison, New Jersey**.
- **Supply Agreement § 5.3:** title and risk of loss pass to Drulun on Delivery. Until then, Pruvax bears all risk, expressly "including during transit" and including temperature excursions.
- **Supply Agreement § 6.2:** Drulun has **30 days after Delivery** to reject nonconforming Product, including Product showing a temperature excursion.
- **Order Form No. 3 § 4.1:** "Delivery" means **tender to the first carrier** at Pruvax's facility at 2100 Ellis Road, Durham, North Carolina, **FCA Pruvax Facility (Incoterms 2020)**. Section 4.2 adds that Pruvax books carriage "on Drulun's behalf," which is consistent with FCA.

**Why the Order Form controls**
- Supply Agreement § 17.3(b) gives the Order Form precedence on "delivery terms." A redefinition of "Delivery" in the Order Form's "Delivery Terms" section falls squarely within that category.
- For the four batches under Order Form No. 3 (OF3-01 to OF3-04, 20,000 vials, **US$8,240,000**), the **Order Form definition likely controls** over Supply Agreement § 1.7.
- Order Form § 1.1 states that it is "governed by the Supply Agreement." That general statement is unlikely to override the specific redefinition, given § 17.3.

**Why it matters to Drulun**
- **Risk of loss shifts to Drulun before cold-chain transit.** Under § 5.3 as applied to the new definition, title and risk pass at Pruvax's dock. A temperature excursion, carrier delay or loss in transit becomes **Drulun's loss**, not Pruvax's, for a refrigerated (2°C to 8°C) oncology injectable worth about US$2.06M per batch. This is the reverse of the protection § 5.3 was written to provide.
- **The rejection window effectively shrinks.** The § 6.2 30-day clock starts at tender in Durham, so transit time comes out of Drulun's inspection period. There is also an argument that an excursion occurring after tender is not a nonconformity "at Delivery." That argument is reinforced by the § 10.2 product warranty, which runs from Delivery.
- **Other knock-on effects:**
  - Title passes in North Carolina.
  - § 4.1 pricing covers carriage only "to the Delivery location." Order Form § 3.2 restates that carriage is included, but the mismatch invites argument.
  - Late-delivery rights (§ 5.4), invoicing (§ 4.3) and Annual Minimum crediting (Order Form § 2.4) all key off the earlier Delivery date.

**Recommended fix**
1. **Check execution status immediately.** Our copy of Order Form No. 3 shows blank signature blocks, and under § 3.3 it binds only once both Parties sign.
   - **If it is unsigned:** strike the § 4.1 definition, or replace it with "Delivery has the meaning given in Section 1.7 of the Supply Agreement," before Drulun signs.
   - **If it is signed:** document a short written amendment to the same effect **before OF3-01 ships** (on or after about January 4, 2027, given the five-business-day early window in § 4.5).
2. **Fallback if Pruvax insists on FCA for logistics reasons.** Keep the FCA shipping mechanics, but state expressly that, notwithstanding § 4.1 and Supply Agreement § 17.3:
   - risk of loss, title and temperature-excursion risk remain with Pruvax until receipt in Edison; and
   - the § 6.2 rejection period runs from receipt in Edison.
3. **Structural fix.** Amend Supply Agreement § 17.3(b) so that an Order Form cannot alter defined terms, risk of loss, title, or inspection and rejection rights unless it expressly refers to the Supply Agreement section being overridden.
4. **Interim protection if the fix is not in place before shipping:**
   - confirm Drulun's cargo and transit insurance covers the shipments;
   - instruct Edison receiving to download and review logger data on arrival; and
   - calendar rejection deadlines from the **tender date**, not the receipt date.

---

### Issue 3 (Medium Priority): DPA Selects Delaware Law and Forum, Splitting Data Claims from Supply Claims

**Where:** Data Processing Addendum, **Section 12 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction)**. Read it with Supply Agreement §§ 15.1 and 17.3(a).

**What the documents say**
- **DPA § 12.1:** the DPA, "and any dispute arising out of or relating to it," is governed by the **laws of the State of Delaware**. The section applies "**notwithstanding Section 15.1 of the Supply Agreement**."
- **DPA § 12.2:** exclusive jurisdiction of **Delaware** state and federal courts.
- **Supply Agreement § 15.1:** New York law and exclusive New York County courts.
- **Supply Agreement § 17.3(a):** the DPA comes first in precedence on Personal Data matters. The conflict is therefore not cured in New York's favor. The Delaware choice **controls for data claims**.

**Why it matters to Drulun**
- **The same event could produce two lawsuits.** The DPA covers patient and reporter data in complaint, adverse-event and serialization records (DPA Recital B; § 2.2). A failure in serialization or complaint intake under Supply Agreement §§ 8.1 and 8.2 can be both:
  - a **supply breach**, governed by New York law and litigated in New York County; and
  - a **data incident**, involving Security Incident costs (DPA § 6.5) and the uncapped DPA indemnity (DPA § 11.1, carved out of the liability cap through § 11.3 and Supply Agreement § 12.3(a)). This would be governed by Delaware law and litigated in Delaware.
- **The practical consequences for Drulun:**
  - **Two forums.** Each is "exclusive," which invites forum fights.
  - **Risk of inconsistent results** on overlapping facts.
  - **Duplicated cost.**
  - **Procedural disputes** over which clause governs a mixed claim.
- **The DPA has no jury waiver or escalation step.** The Supply Agreement's jury waiver (§ 15.3) and executive escalation (§ 15.2) are not replicated in the DPA. Data claims may therefore proceed without either.
- **The DPA indemnity becomes less predictable.** It is likely Drulun's most valuable protection after a breach of patient data, and it would be interpreted under a different body of law from the Supply Agreement terms it cross-references (Supply Agreement §§ 11.3 and 12).

**Recommended fix (either option works; the first is cleaner)**
1. **Conform DPA § 12 to the Supply Agreement:** New York law, exclusive jurisdiction of New York County courts, and the § 15.2 escalation and § 15.3 jury waiver applied to DPA disputes. Delete the "notwithstanding Section 15.1" language.
2. **Alternatively, amend Supply Agreement § 17.3(a)** so the DPA's precedence covers substantive Personal Data obligations only. It would expressly exclude governing law, forum and dispute resolution, which would always be governed by Supply Agreement § 15.
3. In either case, add a sentence requiring **related supply and data claims arising from the same facts to be brought in a single proceeding in New York County**.

Use the DPA amendment mechanism (DPA § 14.1). This can go in the same amendment package as Issues 1 and 2.

---

## 4. Other Observations (Lower Priority)

- **Price adjustment timing.** Order Form § 3.1 states that the US$412.00 price reflects an adjustment notified **May 15, 2026**, "effective for the Contract Year beginning February 1, 2026."
  - Supply Agreement § 4.2 requires **at least 90 days' written notice**, so an adjustment could not properly take effect before about August 13, 2026.
  - The adjustment is also capped by the PPI index change.
  - This does not affect the Order Form No. 3 batches, which deliver in 2027. However, Drulun should check whether Pruvax applied the new price to any invoices for product Delivered before mid-August 2026, and should verify the PPI calculation.
- **Order Form signature status.** As noted under Issue 2, confirm whether Order Form No. 3 has been executed by both Parties. If it has not, Drulun has the cleanest opportunity to fix § 4.1 now.
- **Prior draft (November 2023).** It is superseded and expressly "subject to contract." Its bracketed figures for the cap, Annual Minimum and shortfall rate match the executed terms. No action is needed.

---

## 5. Action Items for Drulun

| # | Action | Owner | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Decide** the commercial goal on term: exit January 31, 2027, a short extension, or renewal on modified terms. | Drulun business and Legal | **Immediately** |
| 2 | Gather the August 14 notice, proof of delivery and receipt, and any earlier written communications about non-renewal. | Drulun Legal | This week |
| 3 | Confirm whether Order Form No. 3 has been signed by both Parties. If not, hold signature pending a fix to § 4.1. | Drulun Supply Chain / Legal | This week |
| 4 | Open negotiations with Pruvax on one amendment package: waiver or extension of term (Issue 1), Delivery definition (Issue 2), DPA governing law and forum (Issue 3), and optionally § 17.3. | Outside counsel, with Drulun | Start by late November; sign **before January 4, 2027** |
| 5 | Interim cold-chain protection for OF3-01: insurance check, logger review on arrival, rejection deadlines calendared from tender. | Drulun Edison DC / Quality | Before first shipment |
| 6 | Calendar the next non-renewal deadline (August 4, 2028, if the Renewal Term stands) with a buffer. | Drulun Legal | Now |
| 7 | Audit 2026 invoices for early application of the US$412 price and verify the PPI cap. | Drulun Finance | Next 30 days |

Please let me know if you would like a draft amendment or a client-facing cover email based on this memo.

---

## 1. Bottom Line

I reviewed the four documents in the matter folder. I found two substantive issues. Both come from the order-of-precedence clause in Supply Agreement Section 17.3. That clause lets two other documents override the New York-law Supply Agreement in defined subject areas.

1. **Highest priority, time-sensitive.** Order Form No. 3 redefines "Delivery" as tender to the first carrier at Pruvax's Durham facility (FCA). The November 2023 draft is superseded and has no operative effect (see Section 5).

**Action items for Drulun:**

## 2. Background and Document Map

| Doc | Description | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Supply Agreement | Manufacturing and Supply Agreement. Effective Date **February 1, 2024** (Preamble; Section 1.8). New York law; exclusive New York County forum (Section 15.1). | Operative |

US$412.00/vial; total US$8,240,000. | Operative once signed by both parties (Supply Agreement Section 3.3; Order Form Section 7.1). Pruvax accepted in writing on September 4, 2026. |

**The order-of-precedence clause (Supply Agreement Section 17.3).** Where the documents conflict, the following order applies:
- (a) the DPA prevails on Personal Data matters;
- (b) the applicable Order Form prevails on Products, quantities, pricing and delivery terms;
- (c) the Supply Agreement comes last.

Both issues below arise because a subordinate document uses this clause to displace a Supply Agreement protection.

## 3. Issue 1 (Highest Priority): Order Form Redefines "Delivery" as Carrier Tender at Pruvax's Dock

**Where:** Order Form No. 3, Section 4.1 (Delivery Terms), read with Supply Agreement Sections 1.7, 5.3, 6.2 and 17.3.

**What the documents say.**
- **Supply Agreement Section 1.7:** "Delivery" means receipt of Product at Drulun's designated distribution center in **Edison, New Jersey**.
- **Order Form No. 3 Section 4.1:** "Delivery" means "tender to the first carrier at Pruvax's facility at 2100 Ellis Road, Durham, North Carolina 27703, **FCA Pruvax Facility (Incoterms 2020)**."
- **Supply Agreement Section 17.3(b):** the Order Form prevails on "delivery terms."

The Order Form's definition therefore displaces the Supply Agreement definition for batches OF3-01 to OF3-04. Order Form Section 1.1 says the Order Form is "governed by the Supply Agreement." That does not cure the conflict, because the Supply Agreement itself tells the reader to apply the Order Form on delivery terms. Section 4.2 reinforces the point: Pruvax books carriage "on Drulun's behalf," which is consistent with an FCA allocation. Drulun should assume Pruvax will rely on the Order Form definition.

**Why it matters to Drulun.** The term "Delivery" drives several key protections in the Supply Agreement. Moving it from Edison to Pruvax's dock changes each of them.

- **Risk of loss in cold-chain transit (Section 5.3).** Title and risk pass "on Delivery." Today, Pruvax "bears all risk of loss of, damage to, or temperature excursion affecting the Product, including during transit." Under the Order Form, risk passes when the shipper is handed to the carrier in Durham. Drulun would then bear any temperature excursion, delay, theft or damage on the road to New Jersey. This product is a 2°C to 8°C refrigerated oncology injectable that must not be frozen, so transit is exactly where the risk lies. Each batch is worth about **US$2.06 million**.
- **Rejection window (Section 6.2).** Drulun has 30 days "after Delivery" to reject nonconforming product, including product showing a temperature excursion. Under the Order Form, the clock starts at Pruvax's dock, not on receipt. Transit days come out of Drulun's inspection time. Pruvax may also argue that an excursion during transit occurred after Delivery, so the product was conforming when Delivered and the loss is Drulun's.
- **Product warranty (Section 10.2).** Pruvax warrants conformity "at Delivery." With Delivery at Durham, Pruvax's warranty arguably does not cover degradation that occurs in transit.
- **Late delivery and the delivery window (Supply Agreement Section 5.4; Order Form Section 4.5).** Pruvax can meet the delivery window and avoid the 30-day-late cancellation right by tendering to the carrier on time, even if the product arrives in Edison late.
- **Invoicing and payment timing (Supply Agreement Section 4.3; Order Form Section 3.4).** Pruvax may invoice "on or after Delivery." Invoicing at tender starts Drulun's 45-day payment period before Drulun has the product or has inspected it.
- **Carriage cost ambiguity.** Supply Agreement Section 4.1 includes carriage "to the Delivery location" in the price. If the Delivery location is Durham, Pruvax could argue that freight to Edison is outside the price. Order Form Section 3.2 helps Drulun because it says the price includes "carriage." The tension is still worth closing.
- **Insurance.** Drulun should confirm whether its cargo or stock-throughput coverage responds to transit risk it did not expect to carry.

**Recommended fix.**
1. **Amend Order Form No. 3** with a short signed amendment under Supply Agreement Section 17.4. The amendment should do one of the following:
   - delete Section 4.1 and replace it with: "'Delivery' has the meaning given in Section 1.7 of the Supply Agreement (receipt at Drulun's distribution center in Edison, New Jersey)"; or
   - add: "Notwithstanding Section 17.3 of the Supply Agreement, the definition of Delivery in Section 1.7 of the Supply Agreement, and Sections 5.3, 6.2 and 10.2 of the Supply Agreement, control." The amendment should also make clear that the Incoterms reference does not shift risk, title or the rejection period.
2. **Fix the template going forward.** Amend Supply Agreement Section 17.3(b) so that an Order Form may not change defined terms, risk of loss, title, or inspection and rejection rights unless it expressly refers to the Supply Agreement section being overridden.
3. **Fallback if Pruvax resists.** At a minimum, require all of the following:
   - risk of temperature excursion stays with Pruvax until receipt in Edison;
   - the 30-day rejection period runs from physical receipt in Edison;
   - the Section 10.2 warranty applies at receipt;
   - Pruvax carries transit insurance naming Drulun as loss payee.

**Urgency.** The first batch (OF3-01) ships for a January 11, 2027 requested delivery date, roughly eight weeks from today. Drulun should raise this with Pruvax now and aim to have a signed amendment before OF3-01 is tendered. Drulun's supply chain and quality teams should also stop signing any future Order Form that contains the FCA language.

---

## 4. Issue 2 (Significant): DPA Selects Delaware Law and Courts and Overrides the Supply Agreement

**Where:** DPA Section 12 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction), read with Supply Agreement Sections 15.1 and 17.3.

**What the documents say.**
- **Supply Agreement Section 15.1:** the Supply Agreement and any related dispute are governed by the **laws of the State of New York**. The parties submit to the **exclusive jurisdiction of state and federal courts in New York County**.
- **DPA Section 12.1:** the DPA and any dispute "arising out of or relating to it" are governed by "**the laws of the State of Delaware** … This Section 12.1 applies **notwithstanding Section 15.1** of the Supply Agreement."
- **DPA Section 12.2:** exclusive jurisdiction lies with the state and federal courts located in Delaware.
- **Supply Agreement Section 17.3(a):** the DPA prevails "on Personal Data matters."

Because the DPA expressly overrides Section 15.1 and the Supply Agreement gives the DPA priority on Personal Data matters, the conflict is not resolved in favor of New York. The Delaware choice likely controls any claim relating to Pruvax's processing of personal data. That includes claims for Security Incidents (DPA Section 6), cost reimbursement (DPA Section 6.5) and Pruvax's data indemnity (DPA Section 11.1).

**Why it matters to Drulun.**
- **Split proceedings.** Many realistic failure scenarios involve both supply obligations and data obligations. Examples are a serialization exception affecting patient-linked unit data (Supply Agreement Section 8.1; DPA Section 2.2(b)), or a missed or mishandled serious adverse-event report (Supply Agreement Section 8.2; DPA Section 2.2(a)). The supply side of such a claim belongs in New York County under New York law. The data side belongs in Delaware under Delaware law. Each forum's clause is "exclusive." That creates the following risks:
  - inconsistent results on the same facts;
  - duplicated litigation cost;
  - threshold fights over which clause governs which claim, with Pruvax able to choose the characterization that suits it.
- **Interaction with the liability regime.** DPA Section 11.3 imports Supply Agreement Section 12 (the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion) and treats the DPA indemnity as uncapped under Section 12.3(a). A Delaware court would interpret those imported New York-drafted provisions under Delaware law. That adds uncertainty about whether the uncapped indemnity and the consequential-damages carve-outs will be read as Drulun expects.
- **Lost procedural protections.** The DPA has no equivalent of the Supply Agreement's executive escalation step (Section 15.2) or its jury waiver (Section 15.3). Data claims could therefore go straight to a jury in Delaware, while related supply claims proceed in a bench forum in New York.
- **Severity.** The data at issue includes patient health information: medical history, concomitant medications, and adverse-event descriptions (DPA Schedule 1). A Security Incident could bring regulatory exposure and notification costs. Those are the claims where Drulun most needs a predictable path to recovery from Pruvax.

**Recommended fix.**
1. **Preferred:** amend DPA Section 12 so that the DPA is governed by New York law and subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with Supply Agreement Section 15.1. Delete the "notwithstanding Section 15.1" language. Extend Supply Agreement Sections 15.2 and 15.3 to DPA disputes.
2. **Alternative or additional:** amend Supply Agreement Section 17.3(a) to state that the DPA's precedence on Personal Data matters does not extend to governing law, forum, dispute resolution or limitation of liability, and that Section 15 of the Supply Agreement governs all disputes under any of the documents.
3. **Belt and braces:** add a consolidation clause providing that any dispute arising under both the Supply Agreement and the DPA from the same facts will be heard in a single proceeding in New York County under New York law.

**Urgency.** This issue is not tied to a deadline, but it should be fixed before any incident arises. It is a natural item to package with the Order Form No. 3 amendment in a single amendment discussion with Pruvax. Pruvax has little principled reason to resist, since neither party is located in Delaware: Pruvax is a North Carolina LLC and Drulun is based in New Jersey.

---

## 5. November 2023 Draft: No Action Required

The November 2023 draft is marked "Superseded by the executed Manufacturing and Supply Agreement dated February 1, 2024," "Draft for discussion purposes only" and "Subject to contract." It has no operative effect. Its substantive terms match the executed agreement. The only differences are bracketed placeholders (the Effective Date, the US$10,000,000 liability-cap floor, the 60,000-vial Annual Minimum and the 35% shortfall rate) and minor wording in Section 2.1.

The draft is useful only as background. It shows that the Edison "Delivery" definition (Section 1.7) and the New York governing-law clause (Section 15.1) were part of the original bargain. That history supports Drulun's request that Pruvax conform the Order Form and the DPA to those terms. Nothing in the draft should be relied on as a source of rights.

---

## 6. Summary Table (Ranked)
